title: Python
principle: Name → object; mutable values can be shared.
notes: Use a context manager for files.
Prefer small functions with explicit inputs.

title: NumPy
code:
import numpy as np
X = np.array([[1., 2.], [3., 4.]])
X.mean(axis=0)  # [2., 3.]
X @ np.array([2., 1.])  # [4., 10.]
notes: Use a seeded default_rng for simulations.

title: Pandas
principle: Validate grain and keys before every merge.
code:
import pandas as pd
df = pd.read_csv("sales.csv")
revenue = df.groupby("region")["amount"].sum()
joined = df.merge(customers, on="customer_id",
                  validate="many_to_one")
notes: Use .loc for explicit row and column selection.

title: SQL
principle: FROM → WHERE → GROUP BY → HAVING → SELECT → ORDER BY
notes: Use a deterministic tie-breaker in ordering.

title: Statistics
principle: Standard error of the mean: s / √n
code:
import numpy as np
x = np.array([2., 4., 6., 8.])
mean = x.mean()
sd = x.std(ddof=1)
se = sd / np.sqrt(len(x))
notes: A p-value is conditional on the null model.
Independence assumptions matter more than large n.

title: Probability
principle: P(A | B) = P(B | A) P(A) / P(B)
code:
prior = 0.01
sensitivity = 0.90
false_positive_rate = 0.05
posterior = (sensitivity * prior) / (
    sensitivity * prior +
    false_positive_rate * (1 - prior)
)

title: Linear Algebra
code:
import numpy as np
X = np.array([[1., 1.], [1., 2.], [1., 3.]])
y = np.array([2., 3., 4.])
beta = np.linalg.lstsq(X, y, rcond=None)[0]
notes: Solve linear systems instead of computing inverses.

title: Calculus
code:
theta = 3.0
eta = 0.1
for _ in range(20):
    gradient = 2 * theta
    theta -= eta * gradient
notes: The gradient has one coordinate per parameter.
A zero gradient can also indicate a saddle point.

title: Machine Learning
principle: Split → fit preprocessing → fit model → validate
code:
from sklearn.pipeline import make_pipeline
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
model = make_pipeline(StandardScaler(),
                      LogisticRegression())
model.fit(X_train, y_train)
notes: Keep the final test set untouched.

title: Model Metrics
notes: Use scores, not hard labels, for ranking metrics.
MAE uses the same units as the target.
Check calibration if probabilities drive decisions.

title: Scikit-learn
principle: Put all learned transforms inside the pipeline.
code:
from sklearn.model_selection import cross_val_score
# model includes preprocessing and estimator
scores = cross_val_score(
    model, X, y, cv=5, scoring="roc_auc"
)
notes: Choose group or temporal splits when needed.

title: PyTorch
principle: Forward → loss → zero gradients → backward → step
code:
import torch
model = torch.nn.Linear(3, 1)
optimizer = torch.optim.AdamW(model.parameters())
x = torch.randn(8, 3)
y = torch.randn(8, 1)
loss = ((model(x) - y) ** 2).mean()
optimizer.zero_grad()
loss.backward()
optimizer.step()
notes: Use model.eval() plus inference_mode() at inference.
CrossEntropyLoss expects logits, not softmax probabilities.
